zh: 9. 现代志癖（modernariat）

en: The excess of memory, which without doubt characterises the contemporary situation, has a name:
. This latter, rather than remaining a fundamental and yet hidden characteristic of the mnestic faculty, breaks through to the surface and is explicitly manifest. What is excessive is not
the split in every instant between a perceived ‘now’ and a remembered ‘now’, but rather the fact that this split has become fully

visible. To what do we owe such a radical disclosure? Perhaps to a pathological ‘lack of attention to life’, as Bergson claims? Nothing of the kind. The memory of the present, whose peculiar function is precisely to represent the possible, presents itself unreservedly when the experience of the possible assumes a crucial importance in the fulfilment of life’s tasks. It is the objective pre-eminence of the virtual in any given type of praxis that brings the mnestic mechanism openly into relief – in determining the temporality of the virtual, this mechanism opens the way to the virtual itself. The excess of memory
induce lethargy and resignation, but on the contrary guarantees the most intense alacrity.
zh: 毫无疑问，记忆过剩是当代处境的特征；而这种过剩有一个名字：对当下的记忆。对当下的记忆不再只是记忆官能中根本却隐蔽的特征，而是突破到表面，明确显现。过剩的并不是每个瞬间本身分裂为一个被知觉的“现在”和一个被记住的“现在”，而是这种分裂变得完全可见。我们为何会经历如此彻底的揭示？或许是因为柏格森所说的病理性“缺乏对生命的注意”？完全不是。对当下的记忆，其独特功能恰恰是表象可能；当可能性经验在完成生命任务时取得决定性重要性，对当下的记忆便毫无保留地显现出来。潜在态在某种实践中的客观优先地位，使这个记忆机制公开凸显；这个机制通过规定潜在态的时间性，为潜在态本身开辟道路。记忆过剩不会导致昏沉和屈从；恰恰相反，它保证了最强烈的敏捷和活力。

en: The paralysis of action, often accompanied by an ironic disillusionment, derives above all from the inability to bear the experience of the possible. To put it another way, the effective cause of this paralysis is the overturning of the memory of the present in

, which, as we know, reconfigures today’s possible as a previously-existing real that we must now inevitably reiterate. Since the memory of the present is an explicit, pervasive phenomenon, even its direct negation – that is, false recognition – is immediately in evidence. Déjà vu is, indeed, a pathology: but, we must add, it is a
pathology.
zh: 行动的瘫痪往往伴随着带有反讽意味的幻灭；它首先源于人们无法承受可能性经验。换一种说法，造成这种瘫痪的实际原因，是对当下的记忆翻转为错误再认；我们知道，错误再认把今日之可能重新塑造成一种先前已经存在、而我们现在不可避免地必须再现的实在。由于对当下的记忆已经成为明确而无处不在的现象，它的直接否定——即错误再认——也立即变得显而易见。既视感确实是一种病理；但必须补充说，它是一种公共病理。

en: In the contemporary situation, apparently in harmony with the plot of the second of Nietzsche’s

, the over-abundance of memory entails an over-abundance of history. This does not, however, mean the maniacal (and asphyxiating) predominance of historiographical studies. The problem is something rather more extreme: the unprecedented proximity of every particular instance of action and suffering to history’s
conditions of possibility, namely what
action and suffering
zh: 在当代处境中，记忆过剩导致历史过剩，这表面上与尼采《不合时宜的沉思》第二篇的论述脉络一致。不过，这并不意味着史学研究狂热而令人窒息地占据支配地位。问题要极端得多：每一次具体的行动和受苦，都以前所未有的方式逼近历史的可能性条件，也就是逼近那个使行动和受苦本身成为历史性的东西。

en: Let us retrace in shorthand a reasoning that we have already worked through in some detail. The memory of the present produces an anachronism. But, mind, only a
anachronism: it gives the present the

of the ‘back then’. Remembering an action as I am carrying it out, I situate it in an undefined past without any date, a past that has never been present. This non-chronological ‘before’ is the faculty, or disposition, on which the execution of this action depends. Because of the formal anachronism, within the event now underway I can simultaneously glimpse both the act and the potential: the language and the word that is uttered, a particular pleasure and the disposition to enjoy pleasure. All the same, when we consider both the specific performance and the faculty that allows for it, we also note their indelible

: language is never realised by the sum of words spoken (in other words, it is never actual); labour-power cannot be equated to the sum of completed labours. And yet, the permanent difference between capacity-to-do and
provides the very foundation of the historicity of experience. The formal anachronism is a representation of this foundation.
zh: 让我们简要重述此前已经详细展开的论证。对当下的记忆会产生时代错置，但请注意，它只产生形式的时代错置：它把“那时”的形式赋予当下。当我在实行一项行动之际记住它，我便把它安置到一个没有日期的不确定过去，安置到一个从未成为现在的过去。这个不属于年代顺序的“之前”，就是该行动之实行所依赖的官能或禀赋。借助形式的时代错置，我能够在当前事件中同时瞥见实现与潜能：语言与说出的词，某种特定快感与享受快感的禀赋。然而，当我们同时考察具体表现和使它成为可能的官能时，也会注意到二者之间不可磨灭的差别：语言从不会被全部已经说出的词实现（换句话说，它从来不会成为完全现实的东西）；劳动力也不能被等同于全部已经完成的劳动。然而，行动能力与既成事实之间的永久差别，恰恰构成经验之历史性的基础。形式的时代错置就是对这一基础的表象。

en: But what matters more: in our epoch, the root of acting historically (the coexistence of, as well as the discrepancy between, potential and act) has acquired empirical and even pragmatic significance as a phenomenon. There is no work task today that does not require – if it is to be discharged in full – the exhibition of the generic psycho-physical disposition to produce (namely, labour-power), which goes beyond the task itself. Nor is there any effective, pertinent discourse today that, beyond communicating

something, does not also have to demonstrate the speaker’s linguistic competence pure and simple, namely the capacity-to-speak (language), which always exceeds the content that the communication happens to have. The formal anachronism thus also itself becomes a

mechanism, an inevitable requisite of production and discourse. The over-abundance of history (connected to the over-abundance of memory) points us to where human praxis is directly grappling with the difference between faculty and performance, which constitutes history’s condition of possibility.
zh: 更重要的是：在我们的时代，历史性行动的根源——潜能与实现的共存及其差距——已经作为现象取得经验意义，甚至实践意义。今天，没有任何劳动任务能够在不展示那种超出任务本身的、进行生产的一般身心禀赋（也就是劳动力）的情况下得到充分完成。同样，今天也不存在任何有效而切题的话语，能够只传达某个内容，而不同时证明说话者单纯的语言能力，也就是那种永远超出偶然传达内容的言说能力（语言）。因此，形式的时代错置自身也成为公共机制，成为生产和话语不可避免的要求。与记忆过剩相关的历史过剩，指向这样一种处境：人类实践直接同官能与表现之间的差别打交道，而这种差别正是历史的可能性条件。

en: Nietzsche held that ‘at the point of a certain excess of history, life crumbles and degenerates – as does, ultimately, as a result of this degeneration, history itself, as well’. We can here put our own name to this statement, on condition that the original meaning is altered. The idea of an ‘end of history’ is
the consequence of excess, as Nietzsche hypothesises,

rather the consequence of its obfuscation. It is also true, moreover, that this obfuscation presupposes a revelation: it concerns something (namely, the over-abundance of history) on which our gaze is now fixed. Let us consider these two aspects more closely. The post-historical state of mind is awakened by the overturning of the (historicising) formal anachronism in the

, which is symmetrically opposed to it. The real anachronism conceals the difference between potential and act (the foundation of historicity), thus reducing potential to a previous act, a faculty to past performances, and language to already-spoken words. Nonetheless, the radical difference between capacity-to-do and
is subject to a transfiguration – one that conceals this difference – precisely and only when it comes to the fore, when it is

empirically most dazzling. The real anachronism is based on the formal anachronism, attesting to its opposite as it clashes with and deforms it. The impression that the historical process is stuck (‘history itself … crumbles and degenerates’) does indeed arise when human praxis stands closest to history’s condition of possibility (‘a certain excess of history’), but it arises as a reaction that detracts from it, or what Dante called a
zh: 尼采认为，“历史一旦过度到某一点，生命便会崩坏和退化；而这种退化最终也会使历史本身同样崩坏”。我们可以在改变原意的条件下，把自己的名字签在这句话下面。“历史终结”观念并不像尼采所设想的那样是过剩的结果，而是遮蔽过剩的结果。此外，这种遮蔽确实又以一次揭示为前提：它所涉及的，正是我们如今目光紧盯的某个东西，也就是历史过剩。让我们更仔细地考察这两个面向。后历史心境，是由使之历史化的形式时代错置翻转成与它对称相反的现实时代错置唤起的。现实的时代错置遮蔽潜能与实现之间的差别——即历史性的基础——从而把潜能还原为先前的实现，把官能还原为过去的表现，把语言还原为已经说出的词。然而，行动能力与既成事实之间的根本差别，恰恰而且只有在它走到前景、在经验上最为耀眼之时，才会遭受一种掩饰差别的变形。现实的时代错置以形式的时代错置为基础；它在同后者冲突并使之变形时，反而为自己的对立面作证。历史进程陷入停滞——“历史本身……崩坏和退化”——的印象，确实在人类实践最接近历史的可能性条件——“历史过剩到某一点”——之时出现；但它作为一种削弱该条件的反应出现，也就是但丁所谓的对称惩罚（contrapasso）。

en: Here, we get to something else that perhaps ought to be counted among the many ways in which we can formulate the salient problem of the contemporary situation. Namely, learning to experience the memory of the present (or better, its explicit, pervasive character) as such, thus liberating it from the nemesis that degrades it into false recognition. Learning to experience the memory of the present means to attain the possibility of a

. Such a possibility, if it is not incarnated in a set of habits – that is, in an ethos – will not remain neglected, ever-flickering on the horizon, but rather penetrates into its opposite, taking on the semblance of the ‘end of history’. And that is what is happening today, in the main. Faced with the hyper-historicity of experience, postmodern ideology hurries to play the broken record of the déjà vu, simultaneously both sweet and gloomy. Everything has already been; history has fallen ‘into the order of the recyclable’; we are destined, for better or for worse, to ‘the massive recall, at every moment, of all the patterns of our life’;
every action has the status and the mannerisms of a quotation.
zh: 到这里，我们触及了当代处境之关键问题的另一种表述方式；或许它应当被列入众多可能表述之中。这个问题就是：学会把对当下的记忆——更准确地说，把它明确而无处不在的性质——作为它本身来经验，从而使它摆脱那个把它贬低成错误再认的惩罚性逆转（nemesis）。学会经验对当下的记忆，意味着取得一种充分历史性存在的可能。这样的可能如果没有体现为一套习惯，也就是一种伦理习性（ethos），就不会只是遭到忽视、永远在地平线上闪烁不定；它反而会渗入自身的对立面，采取“历史终结”的外观。今天，大体上正在发生的正是这种事情。面对经验中高度凸显的历史性（hyper-historicity），后现代意识形态急忙播放既视感那张既甜蜜又阴郁的破唱片：一切都已经发生；历史已经落入“可回收之物的秩序”；不论好坏，我们注定要“在每个时刻大规模召回我们生活的所有模式”；
每项行动都具有引文的地位和腔调。

en: Making its mark on the contemporary public spirit, the déjà vu (or false recognition, or real anachronism)

determines collective behaviours, lifestyles and emotional propensities. To illustrate these behaviours, lifestyles and propensities in a synthetic (yet not elusive) manner, it is opportune again to turn to the second of Nietzsche’s
. We know already that the déjà vu subjects us to a

-past, the fictitious ‘back then’ that the present seems compelled zealously to reproduce. But every relationship with the past, even when it is utterly illusory, requires the development of a certain

. Obviously what is in question here is not a scientific methodology, but an undertone of common sense, the non-premeditated inclination to take care of what has been. The question that makes us again turn to Nietzsche’s text is more or less the following: what kind of ‘historiography’ appertains to the false past set up by déjà vu? What type of historical narration establishes itself at the ‘end of history’?
zh: 既视感（或错误再认，或现实的时代错置）在当代公共精神上留下印记，决定集体行为、生活方式和情感倾向。为了以综合而又不含混的方式说明这些行为、生活方式和倾向，适宜再次转向尼采《不合时宜的沉思》第二篇。我们已经知道，既视感使我们屈从于一个伪过去，屈从于当下仿佛必须热切复制的虚构“那时”。但是，同过去的每一种关系——哪怕纯属幻觉——都要求发展某种史学才能。这里显然不是指科学方法，而是指常识的一种底色，指一种未经预谋便会照料既往之物的倾向。使我们再次转向尼采文本的问题大致如下：哪一种“史学”属于既视感建立的虚假过去？在“历史终结”处确立的，又是哪一种历史叙事？

en: Nietzsche discerned three possible approaches to the cadaster of
. He termed
that history (read: historiography) which strives to present models worthy of emulation: ‘a collection of “effects in themselves” of events that will have an effect in every age’.
history is that concerned with ‘passing judgment on and destroying the past’: it is cultivated by those of us who, unable to bear the miserable present, attempt ‘to give ourselves
, as it were, a new past from which we would prefer to be descended, as opposed to that past from which we actually descended’.
Finally (though taking the middle place in Nietzsche’s ordering), there is
history, which ‘preserves
and venerates’ the past, as it really was, in its totality, without missing out the slightest detail.
For the antiquarian historian,

deserves to be kept alive in memory: the village fête, an incidental comment that just slipped out, the humble ‘almost vanishing traces’ of history. Monumental historiography can degenerate into overblown rhetoric, and the critical approach into peevish rancour: however, since each of them maintains a certain link with activity and the unfolding of history, their over-abundance is harmful to life to only a limited degree. Only the excess of antiquarian history causes irreparable damage. Its stunning suggestion that we ought to remember every particular raises the spectre of hypermnesia, which Nietzsche discusses right at the beginning of this text: ‘Imagine the most extreme example, a human being who does not possess the power to forget.’
This extreme case, at first brought up as a bogeyman, becomes a
when antiquarian history has its way. It flourishes untroubled even ‘when history itself is lost’ – even and
then.
zh: 尼采区分了对待既成事实地籍册的三种可能方式。第一种是纪念碑式历史（monumental history；这里的历史应理解为史学），它努力呈现值得效仿的范型：“由在每个时代都会产生影响的事件之‘效果本身’组成的集合”。
第二种是批判式历史（critical history），它致力于“审判并摧毁过去”；那些无法忍受悲惨当下的人培养这种历史，试图“事后为自己提供一个新的过去，使我们宁愿成为这个过去的后裔，而不是我们实际出身的那个过去的后裔”。
最后（尽管在尼采的排列中居于第二位）是古物收藏式历史（antiquarian history），它“保存并敬奉”过去本来的整体，不漏掉最细微的细节。

对于古物收藏式历史家，一切都值得在记忆中保存活力：村庄节庆、偶然脱口而出的评论、历史中卑微而“几乎消失的痕迹”。纪念碑式史学可能退化为夸张修辞，批判方式也可能退化为乖戾怨恨；不过，两者都同活动和历史展开保持某种联系，因此它们的过剩对生命造成的损害尚且有限。只有古物收藏式历史的过剩会造成不可挽回的伤害。它那种认为每个细节都应当被记住的惊人暗示，唤出了记忆亢进的幽灵；尼采在文章开头就讨论了这种幽灵：“试想一个最极端的例子：一个没有遗忘能力的人。”
这个起初被当作吓人怪物提出的极端个案，在古物收藏式历史得势时变成了日常惯例。即使“历史本身已经失落”，它仍会不受干扰地蓬勃生长——甚至尤其是在这时。

en: The pseudo-past, when we are being led on by the déjà vu, does not allow for filters or choices. Rather, it appears to be ‘preserving and venerating’ everything, almost as if it were a vivid

. Antiquarian historiography lovingly tends to the ‘once upon a time’ evoked by false recognition. But, we should repeat, here ‘historiography’ must not be taken to mean a specialist knowledge, but rather a widespread and even banalised existential attitude. Correlating extremely closely to the post-historical mood, the antiquarian attitude is an indelible component
of the forms of life characterised by the déjà vu as public pathology. But of what, exactly, does this attitude consist?
zh: 当既视感引领我们时，伪过去不容许过滤或选择。相反，它仿佛把一切都“保存并敬奉”起来，就像面对一个鲜活的此时此地。古物收藏式史学满怀爱意地照料错误再认唤起的“从前”。但必须重申，这里的“史学”并非一种专门知识，而是一种广泛流传、甚至已经庸常化的生存态度。古物收藏式态度同后历史心境极为紧密地相关，是那些以既视感这一公共病理为特征的生活形式中不可磨灭的组成部分。然而，这种态度具体由什么构成？

en: The ‘past’ to be preserved and venerated (and this veneration’s only requite is in mimesis) is nothing other than the present: or better, the present smuggled in place of something that already happened, through a real anachronism. Antiquarian historiography applies its own typical methods to actuality: everything that happens is treated as suggestive
, while it is still happening; the current moment is consumed by
. But the antiquarian inclination ought to have a more specific name for when it is concentrated on the present:

. In its common usage, this term designates the – sentimental, aesthetic, commercial – interest in objects and artefacts belonging to the recent past (so recent, it skirts on today): the music of the 1960s, the political posters of the following decade, and then, continuing onward, the washing machine that just gave up the ghost, or last summer’s fashionable hats. In the radical usage that we here propose, ‘modernariat’ instead means the systematic development of an antiquarian sensibility with regard to the

being lived at any given moment. In one sense, the modernariat is a symptom of the doubling of the present as an illusory ‘already-been’; but it also actively contributes to the ever-renewed realisation of this double.
zh: 那个有待保存和敬奉的“过去”——这种敬奉唯一的回报就是模仿——不是别的，正是当下；更准确地说，是借助现实的时代错置，被偷运来冒充已经发生之物的当下。古物收藏式史学把自己的典型方法应用于现实：每件正在发生的事情在尚未结束时，就被当成意味深长的证据；当前时刻被怀旧消耗殆尽。不过，当古物收藏倾向集中于当下时，应当拥有一个更明确的名字：现代志癖。在通常用法中，这个词指向人们对不久以前——近得几乎擦到今天——的物件和人工制品产生的感伤、审美或商业兴趣：20世纪60年代的音乐、下一个十年的政治海报，然后一路延续到刚刚报废的洗衣机或去年夏天流行的帽子。在我们提出的激进用法中，“现代志癖”则意味着：针对每一时刻正在经历的此时此地，系统地发展一种古物收藏式感受力。一方面，现代志癖是当下被复制成幻觉性的“已经发生”这一过程的症状；另一方面，它也积极促使这个复本不断得到重新实现。

en: The modernariat is the historiographical genre that prevails when History always seems to be setting the pace; when, that is, it seems – as Bergson wrote of the déjà vu – ‘that
, that the situation is detached from everything although I am attached to it’.
zh: 当历史看起来总在抢先一步时，现代志癖便成为占据支配地位的史学类型；也就是说，正如柏格森描写既视感时所说，当人觉得“未来已经封闭，情境与一切相脱离，而我却依附于它”时，现代志癖便占据上风。

en: The antiquarian history of the present gives rise to what Nietzsche called ‘a blind mania to collect’.
The modernariat develops a sort of cult of whatever happens to exist

: it surveys it with ‘insatiable curiosity’ and attributes it the stunning fascination and prestige of destiny. Walter Benjamin tried to put some of the prerogatives of the ‘antiquarian’ approach to the service of ‘critical’ history, or to make the antiquariat supremely critical: as such, he sang the praises of the collector (think of his ‘Edward Fuchs, Collector and Historian’

) and his vocation of redeeming the ‘oppressed past’ sabotaged by the victors of history, with special concern for the lowly, the hidden and the silenced. Benjamin’s proposal is, today, being hideously caricatured by part of the modernariat, who favour a particular form of collecting: not to bring out in the present the plot of a thorny past which has been misunderstood (i.e., Benjamin’s intention), but rather to give the present the stigmata of a sacred and unmodifiable past. Not satisfied with contemplating the ‘now’ as if it were a ‘back then’, the post-historical collector also nurtures a certain admiration for it, to the extent of concluding that ‘it’s too late to do anything better’.
zh: 关于当下的古物收藏式历史，产生了尼采所谓的“盲目的收藏狂”。
现代志癖发展出一种对一切恰好在此刻存在之物的崇拜：它以“贪得无厌的好奇心”审视这些东西，并把命运令人震惊的魅力和威望赋予它们。瓦尔特·本雅明曾试图使“古物收藏”方式的某些特性服务于“批判”历史，或者说使古物收藏达到极端批判的程度。因此，他赞颂收藏家（可以想想《收藏家兼历史家爱德华·福克斯》

）以及收藏家拯救“受压迫的过去”的使命；那个过去遭到历史胜利者破坏，收藏家尤其关注其中卑微、隐蔽和被迫沉默之物。今天，本雅明的方案正遭到部分现代志癖者可怕的漫画式歪曲。这些人偏爱一种特殊收藏方式：不是像本雅明所希望的那样，在当下揭示一段棘手而被误解的过去之脉络，而是把神圣且不可更改之过去的圣痕赋予当下。后历史收藏家不仅把“现在”当作“那时”来凝视，还对它怀有某种赞叹，以至最后断定：“现在做得更好已经太迟了。”

en: The antiquarian history of the present, or modernariat, is wholly at one with the
. In turn, we could say that the society of the spectacle is the modernariat raised to the

th degree. The ‘blind mania to collect’ of our time understands the present day as a sort of ‘world’s fair’. An exhibition, that is, where the same individual attends both as an actor (‘playing a role – for most people, many roles, thus playing them all superficially and badly’)
and as a spectator ‘wandering in search of pleasure’. That is, they are their own spectators; or rather, though it is the same thing, they
while it is passing, rather than living it. Why is the present incessantly duplicated as the spectacle of the present? Why does it take on the aspect of a ‘world’s fair’?
zh: 关于当下的古物收藏式历史，即现代志癖，与景观社会（society of the spectacle）完全一致。反过来也可以说，景观社会就是提升到 n 次方的现代志癖。我们时代的“盲目收藏狂”把当今理解为某种“世界博览会”：同一个人在这场展览中既作为演员出席——“扮演一个角色；对大多数人来说是扮演许多角色，因而把每个角色都演得肤浅而糟糕”——又作为“徘徊着寻找快感”的观众出席。也就是说，他们是自己的观众；或者，含义其实相同，他们并非活出自己的生命，而是在生命流逝时收藏它。为什么当下不断被复制成关于当下的景观？为什么它采取“世界博览会”的面貌？

en: Such questions have become rhetorical, by now. The present is duplicated because of the déjà vu. When we feel that we are simultaneously both acting in and spectating on our lives, this is a case of false recognition. It is then, according to Bergson, that a person ‘is looking on at his own movements, thoughts and actions’, such as to split him into two people, as if one were ‘an actor playing a part’ for the other, spectating.
Far from only referring to the growing consumption of cultural commodities, the notion of the spectacle concerns, first and foremost, the post-historical inclination towards

. To put it another way: the spectacle is the form that the déjà vu takes, as soon as this becomes an exterior, public form beyond one’s own person. The society of the spectacle offers people the ‘world’s fair’ of their own capacity to do, to speak and to be – but reduced to already-performed actions, already-spoken phrases and already-complete events.
zh: 到了现在，这些问题已经成为反问。当下之所以被复制，是因为既视感。当我们觉得自己同时在生命中行动，又观看自己的生命时，发生的正是错误再认。柏格森认为，在这时，一个人“观看自己的运动、思想和行动”，以至把自己分裂成两个人，仿佛其中一人为另一个观看着的人“扮演角色”。
景观概念远不只是指文化商品的消费不断增长；它首先涉及后历史式的看着自己生活的倾向。换一种说法：既视感一旦成为超出个人自身、外在而公共的形式，景观就是它所采取的形态。景观社会向人们提供一场展示他们自身行动、言说和存在能力的“世界博览会”——但这些能力已经被还原成做过的行动、说过的语句和完成的事件。
